contents.text_value: This page collects police and court records related to Ben Schneider (Reckless Ben), including American Fork incidents from March 8–11, 2026.
Use Police Records to find the documents and officer profiles for each incident. The Timeline explains the documented roles of the officers and links to the supporting records.

segments.text: to compare synchronized body-camera and dashcam footage from the related encounters, with a searchable transcript and a shared timeline.

contents.text_value: At the October 14, 2026 lawsuit press conference, plaintiffs’ attorney Solomon Radner alleged that Lieutenant Quinn Adamson cut down and seized the GoFundMe sign from a neighbor’s fence on March 11. Radner said the neighbor initially permitted the sign and alleged that police pressured her to withdraw that permission before removing it. This is the plaintiffs’ attorney’s allegation, not a court finding.

contents.label: Solomon Radner’s sign-removal allegation — October 14 press conference (20:40–21:25; Adamson named at 20:52)

sections.title: Criminal Cases
descriptions: Court records associated with Ben Schneider are organized below by jurisdiction and case number.

sections.title: Lawsuit
descriptions: Sheldon David Norcross, Tyler Matthew Shaw, Sierra Nicole Lauts, and Steven Allen filed a federal civil-rights lawsuit against American Fork City and 13 police officers on October 14, 2026. The lawsuit is brought on behalf of these four companions of Ben Schneider (Reckless Ben); Ben Schneider is not a plaintiff. The case is Norcross et al. v. City of American Fork et al., No. 2:26-cv-01008-RJS, in the U.S. District Court for the District of Utah. The complaint contains the plaintiffs’ allegations, not court findings.

segments.text: The complaint and jury demand setting out the four plaintiffs’ claims. This PDF also includes the civil cover sheet.

sections.title: YouTube
descriptions: Selected videos focused on the stops, arrests, Airbnb operation, and police response. Firsthand footage and participant accounts come first, followed by the department’s explanation, attorney analysis, and shorter reporting.

Entries identify the channel and include publication dates and runtimes where available, with a brief description. Legal opinions and allegations in the videos are attributed commentary, not court findings.

contents.text_value: Clearly Established · 18:48 · October 21, 2026. Brandon Grable reviews Sroka’s released September 16 meeting transcript, with interview excerpts featuring Sroka, Steven Allen, Sheldon Norcross, and Solomon Radner. Covers the warrant, transporting detainees, phone seizure, body-camera gaps, redactions, and follow-up.

Clearly Established · 26:46 · October 17, 2026. Daniel Sroka discusses his two meetings with Chief Cameron Paul, including the chief’s changed assessment of the arrests and search warrant, his acknowledgment of mistakes, and public accountability. The video also features interviews with plaintiffs Sheldon Norcross and Steven Allen and their attorney, Solomon Radner.

Brother Counsel (trial lawyer Martin E. Radner) · 34:28 · October 14, 2026. Reaction to the live press conference about the lawsuit filed by four of Ben Schneider’s associates against American Fork City and 13 officers. Includes the plaintiffs’ and their attorneys’ statements, with legal commentary. Ben Schneider is not a plaintiff.
